entities.name: Xu Shuzheng
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Xu Shuzheng (Hsu Seu-cheng; 1880–1925) was a Republican Chinese general and chief lieutenant of Duan Qirui within the Anhui clique, shaping Beiyang politics, the 1918–19 Siberian intervention debates, and the brutal politics of warlord Beijing. A Japan-trained officer, he combined staff skill with ruthless factionalism.

His influence peaked as Duan’s fixer in parliament, finance, and military appointments, making him a hated symbol of Anhui dominance before the Zhili–Anhui War. Assassinated in 1925, he left a legacy of clique militarism that stained early Republican state-building.

Xu is central to understanding Anhui clique power after Yuan Shikai.
